title: org.projectfile.artifacts extension (v1)
description: Standalone contract for the value at the org.projectfile.artifacts subtree — a map of NAMED artifacts a project PRODUCES: the container images it publishes, the packages it ships to a registry, the executables it installs, the services it exposes, the sites it deploys. One neutral home for the question "what does this project give me", answering both a CI tool that needs pointing at an output and a documentation generator that needs to say how to install and call it. Retires the stringly-typed space-separated `M6E_ARTIFACTS` list (which could not say WHICH artifact a given tool wanted) with named keys, so a binary analyzer (gsa) references one artifact and a site auditor (lighthouse) another. Each entry carries a `kind` plus the address fields that kind is addressed by. Referenced from a string anywhere in the document via the §3.8 interpolation sigil: by name for one artifact (`${org.projectfile.artifacts.<name>.path}`), or by the map selector for every artifact of a kind (`${org.projectfile.artifacts{kind=image}.ref}`), which fans a repeating output out to one entry per match.

localizedString.description: BCP 47 language-tagged string map. As a shorthand, a bare string is permitted and treated as { und: <string> } (§7). Inlined rather than referenced across documents so this standalone schema validates with no network fetch, like every other per-namespace schema here — keep it in step with v1.json's own $defs.localizedString.

artifact.description: One thing the project ships. `kind` says what sort of thing it is; the address fields say where to find it. At least one address field (or `ports`) MUST be present — an artifact nothing can be pointed at is meaningless. Which field carries meaning follows from the kind, and the split is deliberate: a consumer pointed at the wrong field resolves nothing rather than a plausible-looking wrong value.

kind.description: What sort of thing this is. The vocabulary is OPEN — a consumer MUST NOT reject a document for an unknown kind — and it MUST NOT change how any lowering (a CI workflow, a build) is generated: for that purpose `kind` is advisory, exactly like a tool's `tags`. It IS load-bearing for documentation and for the `{kind=…}` selector, neither of which is a lowering. Registered kinds and the field each is addressed by: `image` → ref; `binary` → command, path; `package` → registry, name; `module` → module; `service` → ports; `website` → url; `archive` → path. Absent => the artifact is unclassified and no kind selector matches it.

summary.description: One line describing this artifact, for a generator listing what the project provides. Localizable — the sentence is prose, unlike the addresses around it.

path.description: Filesystem path (relative to the project root) of an on-disk output — a built binary a scanner analyzes in place, a release archive. Referenced as `${org.projectfile.artifacts.<name>.path}`.

url.description: A reachable address — what a page auditor (lighthouse / linkinator) fetches. Unlike a webhook secret (named by `${VAR}`), this is a public address committed in the document.

ref.description: A container-image pull reference, registry host included (`kiota.ch/b19/ubuntu/noble:latest`) — what `docker pull` and a Dockerfile `FROM` take. A project publishing one image per matrix cell writes ONE artifact whose ref resolves to several values (via a `{…}` matrix placeholder or a `[]` reference to the axis list), rather than one artifact per cell.

command.description: The executable name this artifact installs as — what a user types. Frequently NOT the project's own name (a project named `bridge` may ship `pf-bridge`), which is why it cannot be inferred and MUST be declared for a generator to document how to invoke the thing.

name.description: The name this artifact is published under in its registry, which is not always the project's name — a scoped npm package (`@scope/thing`), a distribution renamed for PyPI. Distinct from the artifact's own map key, which is its identity WITHIN the document.

registry.description: Which package index `name` is published to: `npm`, `pypi`, `crates`, `maven`, `nuget`, `oci`, … Open vocabulary. It is what lets one selector distinguish two packages of the same kind — `{kind=package,registry=npm}` — so a project publishing to several indexes documents each install command separately.

module.description: An importable / installable module path, in whatever form the language's toolchain takes (`kiota.ch/projectfile/core/v2` for Go). Kept separate from `name` because a module path is a resolvable location while a package name is a registry lookup key.

version.description: The version this artifact is published at, when the document pins one. Usually ABSENT: a released version belongs to the release, not to the source document, and a stale value here is worse than none.

ports.description: The ports a service artifact listens on once it is running. This is the answer to "what do I connect to", which no generic description of a service could supply.

oneOf.description: A bare port number — the whole declaration for a single-port service.
A named port, for a service exposing more than one.

name.description: What this port is for (`api`, `metrics`), so a reader can tell several apart.

protocol.description: Transport protocol. Absent means unspecified rather than tcp — a consumer that needs a default picks its own.
